segments.text: One of the oldest of our fighting forces, with the tradition of courage second to
none, the United States Coast Guard carries the war to the Axis
on the seven seas.
But nowhere do men of the Coast Guard wage more bitter and effective warfare than
in the sub-infested waters of the Atlantic sea lanes.
The U-boats must be battled to the death. The stuff of
production must go through.
For upon the battle of the Atlantic depends the success of assaults in the
making, the success of invasions to come. The men of the Coast Guard do their job
and do it well.
Yes, the Sparrs have a job to do too. Perhaps our jobs are not, for the moment,
so exciting as sending a death charge over a cutter side or seeing a tell-tale
oil slick rise from a blasted sub. But they are vital jobs which must be done.
Vital jobs done by women so that men may fight. That's why you join the Sparrs.
Basic training doesn't take long, only a month, and your pay begins at once. You
learn to take orders and to carry them out.
You acquire new vigor, new confidence. You learn to march
with others and to work with others.
And you learn too that to do your best is the proud tradition of the Coast Guard.
You get good food, plenty of it, and boy how you stow it away.
In school, you learn the lore of ships and aircraft, the language
of the sea, then almost before you know it, you pass in final review,
no longer boot a full-fledged Spar.
Now a man can go to sea. You take over his job
with the same rating, same pay, the same privileges, and the
same responsibilities. These are the jobs which must be done by
Sparrs. Movement of ships and men entrusted to paper is
also entrusted to you.
There are many jobs the Coast Guard needs you for. Each one helps to win this
war. And then too, the skills learned today will mean better jobs tomorrow.
You won't get to be an admiral, but you may be the admiral secretary.
If you are a laboratory technician, dental hygienist, a dietician, an
engineer or a draftsman, the Spars need your knowledge, your skill.
This chemistry major found her birth all right.
Here too, a Spar takes over, and one more pharmacist mate can go to sea.
You may be assigned a duty at one of many busy ports or stations. It may be
Boston or New York, Miami or New Orleans, San Francisco
or Seattle, or even at Coast Guard headquarters in Washington.
As men go to battle, Spars take increasingly important assignments. Radio
technicians are being trained to maintain the Coast Guard's contact between ship
and shore. If you want to hear history in the making, you couldn't pick a better
spot. Out of this room go the commands
to the men on the ships, to the men on the planes, who carry out the missions
which help defeat our enemies.
The mission will be accomplished because the Coast Guard is always ready.
More Spars mean more men on ships. More men on ships mean more
missions accomplished. Join the Spars and release a
man for sea.

reviews.reviewbody: In this curious recruitment film, we're led to believe that doing SPARS work is as exciting as being out at sea with the Coast Guard. Yes, filing, stockroom work, answering phones and typing is just as glamourous as being a gunner! You may even get to work in the Coast Guard Hedquarters! As we see a car pull up, we get excited to see a SPARS rep entering, but WAIT! we see two men get out! The person 'working at the headquarters' is actually the driver! LOL! An interesting film to say the least.
reviews.reviewtitle: No no.. thats SPARS! Not SARS!

reviews.reviewbody:
This WWII recruitment film for the Coast Guard SPARS program (the Guards womens auxiliary) is full of sexist stereotypes and thus is quite campy. The film tells us that by becoming a SPAR, you take over a mans job so he can go to sea and blast Axis submarines. The vast majority of the jobs shown take place in offices and involve typewriters, filing cabinets, and huge rolodexes. If you dont care to work in an office, though, you could dress minor wounds in the dispensary or work in the storeroom! No, you wont become an admiral, but you could be the admirals secretary, is an actual quote from the film. I bet that really packed em in to the recruitment offices. Lots of fun and ripe for msting.
Ratings: Camp/Humor Value: ****. Weirdness: ***. Historical Interest: ****. Overall Rating: ****.
reviews.reviewtitle: Help Smash the Axis by Being a File Clerk!

reviews.reviewbody: The narrator promises us gals that we will "learn the language of the sea..."  Maybe this is why so many gals can cuss like sailors!  Their mamas were SPARS!
